## What changed or decided
- **`snapshot_pr`** now fetches `state,mergedAt,headRefOid,mergeStateStatus` and surfaces `merge_state_status` in the PR state dict.
- **`_merge_or_sync`** (new decision helper) is the single merge-gate choice: when a PR is otherwise ready to merge (all required checks green, Guardian resolved) and `mergeStateStatus == BEHIND`, it returns a new **`sync_branch`** action; every other state (CLEAN/DIRTY/BLOCKED/missing) still returns `merge` unchanged. All **three** merge decision sites (closeout, impl low/medium, impl high/critical via the policy gate) route through it, so a not-otherwise-ready PR is never synced.
- **`_sync_branch`** (new effector): fetches, checks out `origin/<branch>` in a throwaway **detached** worktree (one path serves both impl and closeout PRs), does a plain `git merge origin/<base>` + plain `git push origin HEAD:<branch>` — **no rebase, no force-push**. A conflict runs `git merge --abort` (branch left byte-identical) and stops with a branch-named conflict reason; a push failure is a distinct stop reason; success returns `sync_branch`. Fails closed, never raises.
- Wired `sync_branch` into `ACTION_PRIORITY` (just below `merge`) and `execute_action`. Per the code-review pass, `cmd_loop_run` now **waits after a successful sync** so the new head's checks re-run instead of racing GitHub's eventual consistency.
